What emerges is a snappily staged pantomime, complete with villain, comic sidekicks, love interest, slash-and-bash fight scenes and even a “he’s behind you” moment of sorts, as Hercules sprints across the stage with a monster in hot pursuit.
Hercules, though, is one unit of generic Disney stage entertainment.
Unfortunately, there’s none of the same imaginative energy in this stodgy new stage version, which hits the expected beats without capturing the lovable zaniness that makes Hercules a fan fave.
Hercules is a heroic hit, complete with tunics, thunderbolts, and toe-tapping tunes.
‘Hercules’ is funny and fierce plus ticks all the boxes if you’re looking for a family-friendly mood-lifter.
It’s an enjoyable theatrical production, but struggles to find the sweet spot between being a silly show for kids and a more adult musical about finding your place in the world.
But while it's far from a zero, it's not quite a hero either, and the gospel truth is that the Hercules musical is a mixed bag.
That may induce a sigh from me, but I suspect Joe Tex and family felt they got their money’s worth.
It may put "the glad in Gladiator", but not in my heart.
